candidates.name: Kölner Dom
candidates.price: Admission to the cathedral is free, a 'sightseeing fee' for tourists is being introduced in July 2026 (worshippers and those attending Mass still enter for free). Admission to the South Tower costs €8 (reduced €4, family €20), and admission to the Treasury is also €8 (reduced €4, family €20). A combined ticket for the tower and the treasury is available for €12 (reduced €6, family €30). No luggage or large bags may be carried inside; lockers are available at the nearby station or the service centre
candidates.content: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this monumental cathedral took 632 years to complete, finally being consecrated in 1880. Cologne's Dom is the first thing you will notice when leaving through the main exit of the central station. If

candidates.name: St. Pantaleon's Church
candidates.content: An early Romanesque basilica in the southern part of the Old Town, once serving as the church for a Benedictine abbey. It is dedicated to St. Pantaleon, St. Cosmas, and St. Damian. Sightseeing is restricted to times outside of rel

candidates.name: St. Cecilia's Church
candidates.content: A Staufen-period pillar basilica and one of Cologne's twelve great Romanesque churches. It features notable historical elements such as a 12th-century tympanum and remnants of Ottonian architecture. Since 1956, the church building

candidates.name: Museum für Angewandte Kunst
candidates.price: Regular €4, reduced €2, permanent and special exhibitions: price varies from being free to €6
candidates.content: The Museum of Applied Art has a collection of popular design items, as well as temporary exhibitions. The historical collections have been closed for several years due to refurbishment and new exhibition concept.

candidates.name: Römisch-Germanisches Museum
candidates.content: Römisch-Germanisches Museum explores the history of Roman history in Cologne and the surrounding area. The permanent exhibition is now located in the Belgian House (Cäcilienstraße 46, near Neumarkt). The exhibits of the Dionysos m

candidates.name: NS-Dokumentationszentrum
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-19:00, closed on Mondays
candidates.content: "NS" is short for National Socialist. Former headquarters of the Cologne Gestapo, with prison cells. Now the largest regional memorial site in Germany for the victims of the Nazis. Library, media and exhibitions. Near subway stop

candidates.name: Basilica of St. Cunibert
candidates.content: St. Kunibert is the youngest of Cologne’s 12 Romanesque churches, famous for the Kunibertuspütz. According to local legend, Cologne’s babies are born in this crypt well rather than being delivered by the stork. The church is a tre

candidates.name: Basilica of St. Severin
candidates.content: St. Severin' is the second tallest of Cologne's Romanesque churches (79 m), dedicated to the patron saint of rain who is said to protect the city from drought. Visitors can walk beneath the elevated 19th-century shrine to receive

candidates.name: St. Maria Lyskirchen
candidates.content: St. Maria in Lyskirchen is the smallest of Cologne’s twelve Romanesque churches, famous for its remarkably well-preserved 13th-century ceiling frescoes, the only ones of their kind to survive largely intact in the city. Located ne

candidates.name: St. Andrew's Church
candidates.content: St. Andreas Church is a notable example of the transition from Romanesque to Gothic architecture and contains a 14th-century crypt where the scholar Albertus Magnus is buried. The interior is characterized by a series of contempor

candidates.name: Basilica of the Holy Apostles
candidates.content: A Romanesque basilica featuring a cloverleaf-shaped choir and a 67-meter-high west tower. Sightseeing is only possible outside of service hours. Group tours must be arranged in advance via the parish office; information on public

candidates.name: St. Gereon's Basilica
candidates.content: One of Germany's oldest churches, built on the foundations of a late antique oval structure. It is famous for its unique decagonal dome and elliptical floor plan. Please note that sightseeing is restricted to times outside of reli

candidates.name: Basilica of St. Ursula
candidates.content: One of Germany's oldest continuously used churches, with origins dating back to the Roman era. It is best known for the "Golden Chamber," a historic ossuary, and its significance as a site of pilgrimage. Access for sightseeing is

candidates.name: St. Maria im Kapitol
candidates.content: The oldest and largest of Cologne's Romanesque churches, built upon the foundations of a Roman temple. Its unique floor plan is modeled after the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem and houses treasures such as an 11th-century car

candidates.name: Groß-St. Martin
candidates.content: A landmark Romanesque basilica in the Old Town, characterized by its distinctive trefoil choir and soaring crossing tower. It was founded around 960 AD as a Benedictine monastery. The current structure dates to the 12th and 13th c

candidates.name: St. George's Church
candidates.content: Founded in 1059, this basilica is noted for its Roman-era columns and vaulted architecture that earned it the nickname "Ravenna on the Rhine." It stands on the site of a former Roman guard post. Sightseeing is restricted to times

candidates.name: Museum Ludwig
candidates.hours: Tue–Sun 10:00-18:00, first Thu of the month 10:00-22:00
candidates.content: A museum of modern art, near the central railway station and the Cathedral hosts a worthy regular exhibition and temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud
candidates.price: Permanent collection and special exhibition: €8-12, reduced €4.50-8
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, every 1st and 3rd Thu of the month until 21:00
candidates.content: The Wallraf-Richartz Museum is an art gallery with a collection of fine art from the medieval period through to the early 20th century.

candidates.name: Rautenstrauch-Joest-Museum für Völkerkunde
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, first Thu of the month 10:00-22:00
candidates.content: North Rhine-Westphalia's only ethnological museum, it has a fine collection of Amerindian and Austro-Polynesian artefacts.

candidates.name: Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst
candidates.hours: Tue–Sun 11:00-17:00, first Thu of the month 11:00-22:00
candidates.content: Art, music, books, films and culture from Asia.

candidates.name: Kolumba
candidates.content: A Christian art museum. An architectural wonder designed by Peter Zumthor and a feast for the senses; this museum, built in concordance with the ancient foundations of the shrine of Mary in the rubble contains a selection of histo

candidates.name: Schokoladenmuseum Köln
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun holidays 10:00-18:00, last admittance one hour before closing
candidates.content: Chocolate museum in Cologne. It's a short visit but very interesting exhibits. Admission €13.50, concessions €8.50, family pass €34.50 (surcharge on weekends).

candidates.name: Käthe Kollwitz Museum
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-18:00, closed on Mondays
candidates.content: Dedicated to the artist Käthe Kollwitz (1867-1945), the first woman elected to the Prussian Academy of Arts.

candidates.name: Cologne City Museum
candidates.hours: Tue 10:00 to 20:00, Wed-Sun 10:00 - 17:00, every 1st Thu of each month: 10:00 - 22:00
candidates.content: Shows exhibits and works of art on the history of the city of Cologne from the Middle Ages to the present day.

candidates.name: Die Kölner Synagoge
candidates.content: The Cologne Synagogue is architecturally striking for its dark, monumental style. Its Torah scroll has a significant history, having been rescued by a Catholic priest from another synagogue during the Nazi era. In 2005, Pope Bened

candidates.name: Historisches Rathaus
candidates.content: The Cologne City Hall is Germany’s oldest functioning municipal building, with origins dating back to the 12th century. The complex is defined by the 15th-century Gothic tower, which served as a symbol of the city's guilds, and th

candidates.name: Gürzenich dance hall
candidates.content: The Gürzenich is a municipal concert and event hall, best known for its late Gothic façade completed in 1447. It was built as a venue for public festivities. It retains its historic architectural character while functioning as a m

candidates.name: Hohenzollern Bridge
candidates.content: Also called the Locking Bridge. If you walk to the back of the Kölner Dom along a straight path, there is a bridge on the Rhine to your right that is covered in padlocks. The locks are placed there by couples to show their loyalty

candidates.name: Kölner Zoo
candidates.content: Established in 1860, the zoo of Cologne is home to more than 850 animal species from all over the world. Highlights include the Great Ape Jungle House, the Rainforest Hall, the Aquarium, and the houses for elephants, hippos and cr

candidates.name: KD Rhine River Cruise
candidates.content: Departure times: Daily: 10:30, 12:00, 14:00, 18:00; Köln-Düsseldorf offers cruises of the Rhine river around the Cologne area with an explanation of landmarks.

candidates.name: Stadtgarten
candidates.content: Concert centre for jazz and contemporary music, with a cafe and restaurant inside and a large beer garden outside which dates back to at least the 1950s. (Also the site of a great Christmas market.)

candidates.name: 1. FC Köln
candidates.content: Die Geißböcke ("The Billy Goats") were promoted in 2025 and now play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. The stadium has a capacity of 46,000 and in 2024 hosted matches in the UEFA Finals. The women's team play in their top tier a

candidates.name: Stattreisen e.V.
candidates.content: This non-profit organization offers excellent tours of Cologne, led by volunteers. The prices are moderate and there is a huge list of tours, including (besides the more regular tours) Koelsch tours (for testing the breweries) or

candidates.name: Rickshaws: environmentally friendly city tours
candidates.content: Rickshaws are exotic and environmentally friendly tricycles, that bring their passengers slowly and safely to their destination. By Rickshaw you will discover Cologne’s points of interest in a comfortable way.

candidates.name: Neptunbad
candidates.content: In the popular area of Ehrenfeld in an old renovated bath, to which an attractive "sauna landscape" in Japanese style on two levels has been added. Also a comprehensive fitness centre.

candidates.name: Saunas in public swimming pools
candidates.content: Some of the public swimming pools managed by the Cologne city council, notably Agrippabad, do have small Saunalandschaften too, all featuring a Damentag (ladies only day).

candidates.name: Ananda Tantra Massage and Coaching
candidates.content: Tantra massage, coaching and workshops, an open minded and liberal attitude essential because the massages include sexually sensitive body parts, however, no sexual services are given by the team of 30 female and male employees.

candidates.name: Kölner Philharmonie
candidates.content: Central concert hall, opened in 1986. Main season September to June. Special summer shows.

candidates.name: Oper Köln
candidates.content: Operas are performed in the Staatenhaus while the opera building at Offenbachplatz is being renovated. Season starts in Mid-September.

candidates.name: Aqualand
candidates.content: Water park with water slides, pools, saunas and a wellness area.

candidates.name: Claudius Therme
candidates.content: Large spa with pool and lots of different saunas (indoors and outdoors) next to the Rhine, north of Deutz.

candidates.name: Mauritius Therme
candidates.content: Decent Saunalanschaft in a hotel south of Neumarkt.

candidates.name: Mediterana
candidates.content: 11 saunas and a huge pool.

candidates.name: monte mare Bedburg
candidates.content: Large spa in the west of Cologne.

candidates.name: monte mare Reichshof-Eckenhagen
candidates.content: Spa in the east of Cologne.

candidates.name: Metropolis Cinema
candidates.content: If you want to go to the movies while visiting Cologne and you don't know German, this small cinema is for you. It shows movies in their native language, but mostly English. (However, most other cinemas will also show English vers

candidates.name: Kölner Seilbahn
candidates.price: Adult one way €4.50, return €6.50; child (aged 4–12) one way €2.50, return €3.70
candidates.content: Take a ride with the Aerial tramway across Rhine river.

candidates.name: Sukon - Thai Art Of Massage
candidates.content: Traditional Thai massage institute, in the city centre. Thai native massage therapists practise in the 160-m² Thai-styled studio: original royal massage, aroma oil massage and foot massage. This place does not offer any erotic mas

candidates.name: Sixpack
candidates.content: In the vibrant Belgisches Viertel (Aachener Straße 33 - next to Rudolfplatz) you should be aware to wait long or even get rejected especially at a late hour. Mixed music from Electro to Indie with a huge variety of bottled beer.

candidates.name: Früh am Dom
candidates.content: Früh am Dom is a great place to try the local Kölsch brew.

candidates.name: Brauhaus Gaffel
candidates.content: Beer hall right next to the cathedral, serves food too.

candidates.name: Hellers Brauhaus
candidates.content: Younger crowd.

candidates.name: Brauerei Malzmühle
candidates.content: Visited by Bill Clinton.

candidates.name: Alter Wartesaal
candidates.content: Nifty bar and disco beside the central station: various events & exclusive parties.

candidates.name: Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld & YUCA („Your Urban Club of Arts“)
candidates.content: Club complex in Ehrenfeld. Parties and concerts. Devoted to a variety of international styles including hip-hop, jazz and Latin music.

candidates.name: Bootshaus
candidates.content: Serious clubbing. In an old harbor storage facility, but very modern inside. One of Germany's top clubs.

candidates.name: Gebäude 9
candidates.content: Concerts. International flavor. Alternative crowd. Quite popular. Inside a defunct factory site on the right bank of the river.

candidates.name: Club Subway
candidates.content: Various parties from Hip Hop, Electro to Indie music with a hip but laid back audience (Moltkestraße metro - next to Rudolfplatz).

candidates.name: Thiebolds-Eck
candidates.content: A typical Cologne corner pub, as you would imagine: Rustic interior, worn bar and tables, plenty of decorations, you can meet local football fans here on match days, freshly tapped and ice-cold Reissdorf Kölsch, small but fine Col

candidates.name: Falafel Habibi
candidates.content: Very authentic small Lebanese restaurant with traditional dishes. Kind staff. Delicious food. Good vibes. They have two stores, which serve the same food (though sweetmeats may vary).

candidates.name: Selam
candidates.content: Ethiopian restaurant, opens Tu-F at 17:00 and on weekends at 16:00. Good selection of mild and spicy Ethiopian dishes served on the traditional plate of injera bread.

candidates.name: Brauhaus FRÜH am Dom
candidates.content: Traditional Colognian restaurant. Cologne flair.

candidates.name: Maison Baguette
candidates.content: Fantastic sandwiches, very well served and with incredible bread. Very friendly service. Diverse menu. The owner is nice and you immediately feel at home.

candidates.name: Lizbät
candidates.content: Delicious crepes, a nice ambience and great service. There are all kinds of crepes: vegetarian, vegan, with meat, and sweet. The beer garden is nice and the service is good.

candidates.name: Vegan Revolution
candidates.content: Best makali halloumi sandwich around. Amazing Baba ganoush and hummus. Every item is flavourful and freshly made. It's a small place and has a good quality.

candidates.name: Reissdorf im Moselstübchen
candidates.content: Nice and cozy pub. Small menu with something for everyone. Even vegetarian bratwurst. Simple Colognian pub with good bourgeois cuisine and an always delicious tap Kölsch beer.

candidates.sec: In and around the central train station
candidates.name: Weinhaus Vogel
candidates.content: Real Cologne restaurant. Nice service, good food and tasty beer. A very special ambience.

candidates.name: Curry B.
candidates.content: Very tasty currywurst with fries. Very pleasant place for a quick bite.

candidates.name: Gaumenschmaus
candidates.content: Clean, delicious home-style cuisine. Every day a different menu for lunch. Everything freshly prepared. Good Schnitzel.

candidates.name: Da Nino
candidates.content: A real insider tip for super delicious and authentic pizza. Authentic Italian dishes. Cool place, lovely staff.

december.text: | content=One of the most famous Christmas markets, and a visit highlight for everyone who loves over-the-top Christmas ambience. Late November to December 23.

Stadtgarten: Concert centre for jazz and contemporary music, with a cafe and restaurant inside and a large beer garden outside which dates back to at least the 1950s. (Also the site of a great Christmas market.)
